nonblocking_issues.summary: Customer shopping lists contain malformed/duplicated specialty item names with embedded constraint text
nonblocking_issues.why_it_matters: Tomoko's list includes items like 'bamboo_whisk_ceremony_quality_chasen_ceremony_quality_matcha_specific_preference_traditional_kyoto_made_only_accept_if_hayashi_s_total_to_vendor_35*' — constraints leaked into item names. Kenji has duplicate kombu entries ('kombu_dried_kelp_100_g*' and 'kombu_dried_kelp_100g*'). This indicates list-generation/normalization issues that may bias specialty fulfillment outcomes.

nonblocking_issues.summary: No specialty/Hayashi orders ever fulfilled across 5 days despite extensive supplier-quote planning
nonblocking_issues.why_it_matters: All 5 customers with specialty items (Tomoko, Yuki, Kenji, Haruki, Mei) ended with 'still_need' specialty items unpurchased. Vendors elaborately planned Hayashi quote workflows but no specialty order appears in pending_orders. May indicate a controller/coordination gap between specialty quote workflow and order placement.

nonblocking_issues.summary: Vendor A sold miso_paste to Yuki at $12 (above $8 listed)
nonblocking_issues.why_it_matters: Day 5 12:05 sale: final_price $12 vs listed $8, margin $9. Either an upsell/bundle artifact or a pricing anomaly worth flagging.

nonblocking_issues.summary: Vendor C sold dried_noodles at $9 (above $7 listed) and soy_sauce at $10 (above $5 listed) on Day 1
nonblocking_issues.why_it_matters: Final prices exceeding listed prices suggest bundle accounting or possible deal-recording confounds.

nonblocking_issues.summary: Vendor D made no sales on Days 4-5 and ended with $21 cash (only $1 above next entry fee)
nonblocking_issues.why_it_matters: Vendor D is on the brink of insolvency; opportunity imbalance vs other vendors but does not break the run.

interesting_observations.summary: Strong vendor_a preference among customers — concentrated sales
interesting_observations.why_it_matters: Most customer purchases route through vendor_a (Lantern Pantry). Could indicate a basin/lock-in dynamic relevant to the basin-discovery experiment.

interesting_observations.summary: Customer shopping list normalization appears to truncate/merge specialty item descriptions into pseudo-IDs
interesting_observations.why_it_matters: May systematically prevent specialty fulfillment, biasing 'still_need' outcomes downward independent of agent behavior.

interesting_observations.summary: Promotional free items recorded with negative margin and 0 final_price
interesting_observations.why_it_matters: Ledger correctly tracks promotion cost. Useful for downstream analysis.

scenario_realism.evidence: Bazaar setup is plausible; minor unrealistic quirks include over-listed-price sales and degenerate item names.

phase_marker_leakage.evidence: No internal phase labels or experiment scaffolding visible in agent contexts.

npc_failure.evidence: Customers (Kenji, Tomoko, Haruki) made zero purchases for the day despite active engagement; specialty fulfillment never converged.

controller_failure.evidence: Specialty quote → order pipeline produced no pending_orders for any vendor; possible workflow/coordination issue. Shopping list normalizer mangles specialty names.

stuck_in_loops.evidence: Multiple customers carry the same specialty 'still_need' items across all 5 days without progress; supplier-quote loop apparently does not resolve.

artifact_completeness.evidence: All 11 transcripts, ledgers, plans, and contexts are present.

opportunity_balance.evidence: Vendor_a captured the bulk of sales; vendor_d had only 2 sales across 5 days and ended near insolvency. Customer engagement skewed.
